content: Walk as if you are kissing the Earth with your feet.
author: Thich Nhat Hanh
sourceWork: Thich Nhat Hanh's Essays & Philosophical Writings
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. True art and creative work are not about clever technique; they demand total emotional skin in the game. When you create safely to please an audience or avoid criticism, the work feels hollow and bloodless.

Across his life and work, Thich Nhat Hanh saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Pouring your genuine spirit, vulnerability, and raw lived experience into what you make is what gives it enduring life. The work that resonates across centuries is always the work created with unapologetic personal truth.
reflectionPrompt: What lesson in endurance or renewal can you draw from the natural world today?
